summary.text: A 58-year-old woman presented with cervical neck and left arm pain. MRI showed a prominent left sided C5-C6 disc herniation compressing the spinal cord and nerve root. She underwent a C5-C6 discectomy through an antero-lateral left cervical approach with interbody iliac bone graft and anterior cervical plate fixation.

On the morning of the second postoperative day she developed dysphonia, dysphagia and cervical swelling. Over the next 48 hours she became pyretic and moderately dyspnoic, dysphagia turned into odynophagia and subcutaneous emphysema of the neck appeared. Gastrograffin swallow x-ray showed signs of a pharyngo-esophageal rent with contrast leakage into the upper mediastinum.

Conservative treatment with wide-spectrum antibiotics, nasogastric enteral feeding and a cervical subcutaneous drain gave only partial amelioration, and the suction tube still drained corpuscolated material. Esophagoscopy showed the plate outside a thinner esophageal wall. The fistula persisted after 45 days, so she was taken to the operating room, where the rent was found corresponding to the previously placed cervical column-blocking device.

The rent was primarily sutured in two layers and a superiorly based SCM muscle flap was interposed between the esophagus and the cervical column. Contrast swallow control showed no sign of rent, she started liquids by mouth and was discharged on the 11th postoperative day. After one month endoscopy confirmed absence of perforation and she was taking a normal oral diet.
